summary: Systems engineer developing automated hardware tests, custom bench electronics, and embedded C firmware. Experience spans board qualification, instrumentation, international firmware deployment, and aerospace hardware assembly.

bullets: Own qualification, calibration, and production acceptance across six board families using Python, PyQt6, bench instruments, SCPI, GPIB, and NI-DAQmx for electrical, analog, thermal, telemetry, and firmware testing.
Transitioned board testing to a custom OpenTAP front end and OpenHTF back end, standardizing test workflows and interfaces to improve reliability and scalability.
Developed a custom selector for four electrostatic correction boards; wrote C firmware with SCPI-style commands over RS-485 to route measurement outputs and Ethernet control for the active board.
Investigated power-up IP assignment and connectivity failures surfaced by faster automated testing; used AMD Vivado and register-level analysis to diagnose hardware and firmware faults.

Coordinated overseas and field teams for firmware deployments, arranging scan comparisons before and after upgrades to verify equal or better performance, supplying updated hardware, and guiding remote installation.
Built a Flask and SQLite system of record covering hardware and firmware revisions for more than 90 boards; track configuration conflicts, deployment requirements, and upgrade progress.
Characterized SEM settling with Python signal analysis and tuned inertia compensation, reducing time for oscillations to fall below 2 nanometers from 300 to 20 nanoseconds.

Built Python API and analysis pipelines for Inventory Control and Quality Assurance; migrated anomaly detection to AWS Lambda, EventBridge, and Secrets Manager, reducing estimated annual vendor transaction risk by $100,000.
Automated labor reporting across fulfillment centers with VBA, eliminating over 120 hours of manual work each week.
Modeled structural components in SolidWorks for LuSEE-Night, a NASA-funded lunar radio observatory; fabricated and assembled satellite hardware in cleanrooms under contamination-control protocols.
Assembled high-voltage step-up converters and installed flight-hardware wiring harnesses and passive components.
Built a programmable Verilog timing engine with SPI host control, UART transmit firmware, and Python tooling for reproducible protocol debugging on IHP CMOS5L.
Validated with 200 Python tests, six RTL simulation suites, and formal safety checks; implemented a routed layout targeting 25 MHz, with electrical closure still in progress.
Built weapon and drive power systems integrating motor controllers, brushless motors, wiring harnesses, and battery management; designed packaging to protect electronics from shock and vibration.

coursework: Instrumentation Laboratory, Advanced Experimental Laboratory, Electromagnetism and Optics, Quantum Mechanics, Statistical and Thermal Physics
skills: Oscilloscopes, custom test hardware, PyVISA, AMD Vivado, SolidWorks, cleanroom assembly
Python, C, Verilog, SQL, LabVIEW, pytest, cocotb, Icarus Verilog, GitHub Actions, Linux
